points.t: Referring a skin lesion through a **teledermatology or advice-and-guidance** service.
Images + history are **triaged by a dermatologist**, who can discharge, advise, book surgery directly or fast-track.
**Three views** (regional, close-up with ruler, polarised in-focus dermoscopy) + full history including change and risk factors + consent.
**Poor images**, missing dermoscopy, scalp / genital / nail lesions, and **delay** in a suspected melanoma pathway.

cause.lead: Images travel; the patient doesn’t have to (yet).
points: NHS England **teledermatology roadmap (2023)**: primary-care advice and guidance; **referral triage** (images on all 2WW skin referrals); community **image capture hubs**; **AI-assisted triage** (HTG746).
The dermatologist may discharge, advise, list for surgery, or fast-track.

visuals.caption: Three standard views: regional (where on the body), close-up with a ruler (size and surface), and a polarised, in-focus dermoscopic image of the whole lesion.
visuals.alt: Three frames: forearm location, close-up with ruler, dermoscopy

points: **Dermoscopic image**: polarised, in focus, whole lesion in view.
Good lighting, no flash glare, plain background, patient ID label, consent, secure storage.
Duration, **change**, symptoms, risk factors (sunburn, sunbeds, family history, immunosuppression), 7-point score.
Check focus and framing before sending.
Scalp, genitals, nails: may need face-to-face.
Local teledermatology pathway and image capture standards.
IPs in a PCN may capture images if trained.
Changing lesion (change = 2 + any other) → 2WW **with images**; specialist arranges excision biopsy.
Explain photos may be reviewed first and they may be booked straight for surgery; consent for storage.

limits.t: Refer face to face rather than delay.

items.t: Teledermatology must **not delay** a suspected cancer pathway: poor images → refer face to face.

pearls.t: Three views, every time: where, how big, what structure.
Tell patients they might go straight to surgery.
An AI or app result never overrides clinical concern.

quiz.a: Polarised, in focus, whole lesion in view.

quiz.q: Images poor on a suspected melanoma?
quiz.a: Refer face to face; don’t delay.

quiz.q: What must the patient consent to?
quiz.a: Image capture and storage, and specialist review.
